2026-11-09-oil-steepest-weekly-fall-sinc.angle: Short-run demand for oil is price-inelastic, so even a modest change in supply causes large price swings, which helps explain a 16% fall in one week. If the strait reopens, supply shifts from S1 to S2, the world price falls and the quantity traded rises; markets are pricing this in already. A lower oil price reduces petrol and freight costs, so headline CPI eases and there is less pressure for further RBA rate rises.

2026-11-07-budget-tightening-december-up.title: Should the budget be tightened in December's update?
2026-11-07-budget-tightening-december-up.summary: Weighs the case for and against cutting spending in the December MYEFO while the RBA raises rates, and shows how tightening both policies would shift AD further left.
2026-11-07-budget-tightening-december-up.lede: With the RBA raising rates, some commentators want the government to cut spending in the December mid-year economic update, and ABC political editor Jacob Greber argues it is the right prescription at the wrong time. Minister Clare O'Neil has confirmed a savings package for the update that she called a 'mini budget', with priorities of lower spending, cost-of-living relief that does not add to inflation, and productivity.

2026-11-07-budget-tightening-december-up.angle: The policy mix matters: if fiscal and monetary policy both tighten into a slowdown, the combined effect on growth and jobs could be larger than intended. Higher rates already reduce consumption and investment, and spending cuts would reduce G as well, shifting AD from AD1 to AD2, so the price level eases but real GDP falls and unemployment rises. Case for cutting: spending is above pre-pandemic levels, it would help the RBA reduce inflation, and fiscal policy could share the load with mortgage holders. Case against (Greber): the deficit is already narrowing faster than forecast, the RBA expects business investment to collapse in the second half of 2027, and house prices have fallen more than Treasury expected.

questions.q: Evaluate whether both fiscal and monetary policy should be contractionary in Australia in late 2026.

2026-11-07-budget-tightening-december-up.note: The case against tightening is Greber's argument. Former RBA board member Warwick McKibbin told 7.30 this level of spending is not a problem while inflation and interest rates are low, and Governor Bullock says monetary policy cannot affect global oil prices so the RBA is targeting domestic capacity pressures. The savings package details are not yet known. The diagram is illustrative. UPDATE DUE: the December MYEFO. 2026-11-06-consumer-sentiment-job-fears.title: Consumers deeply pessimistic as job fears rise
2026-11-06-consumer-sentiment-job-fears.summary: Households expect higher unemployment and mortgage rates after five rate rises, and expectations can become self-fulfilling by cutting consumption and shifting aggregate demand left.
2026-11-06-consumer-sentiment-job-fears.lede: The Westpac-Melbourne Institute consumer sentiment index fell 4.2% over the three months to October to 80.4, among the 40 weakest readings since the survey began in 1973, and the unemployment expectations index jumped 9.3% to 142.2. CommBank now expects GDP growth to slow to 1% by mid-2027 (previously 1.8%) and unemployment to peak at 5.1% at the end of 2027, up from 4.7% now.

2026-11-06-consumer-sentiment-job-fears.angle: Expectations can be self-fulfilling: if households fear job losses they save more and spend less, which reduces aggregate demand and can lead to the job losses they feared. Lower consumer confidence and higher interest rates reduce consumption, so AD shifts from AD1 to AD2; the price level eases, which helps bring inflation down, but real GDP falls and unemployment rises.
